results.description: You are an Eliashib — someone who leads by jumping in first. When work needs to be done, you do not wait for instructions or committees. You roll up your sleeves and start building, inspiring others through your personal example and willingness to get your hands dirty. Your enthusiasm is contagious, and people follow you because they see you doing the work yourself. Your initial passion and dedication set the tone for everything that follows.
strengths: Willingness to lead by example and work alongside others
Natural ability to inspire people through personal dedication and energy
Courage to take the first step when others are still deliberating
Humility to do manual work regardless of your position or title
watchFor: Allowing personal relationships to compromise your integrity or mission
Starting strong but failing to maintain vigilance over time
Accommodating people who oppose God's work because of family or social pressure
Letting initial zeal substitute for sustained, disciplined faithfulness

scripture.text: Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests went to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They dedicated it and set its doors in place.

results.title: The Bold Challenger
results.description: You are a Sanballat type — but redeemed. You have a sharp eye for problems, a bold voice, and zero tolerance for what you see as weakness or foolishness. In its shadow form, this becomes destructive criticism and opposition. But when submitted to God, your gift for spotting vulnerabilities, your courage to speak uncomfortable truths, and your strategic mind become powerful tools for protecting and strengthening what God is building. The difference between a Sanballat and a prophet is whose side you are on.
strengths: Ability to identify weaknesses and vulnerabilities others miss
Courage to speak difficult truths that need to be heard
Strategic thinking and ability to anticipate problems before they arise
Persistence and determination that does not back down under pressure
watchFor: Using your critical eye to tear down rather than build up
Opposing change simply because it threatens your comfort or position
Mistaking cynicism for wisdom and criticism for discernment
Building coalitions against people rather than for God's purposes

scripture.text: As iron sharpens iron, so one person sharpens another.

results.title: The Empowering Provider
results.description: You are an Artaxerxes — someone whose greatest contribution is empowering others to fulfill their calling. You may not be the one laying bricks, but you provide the resources, authority, protection, and open doors that make the work possible. Your influence, generosity, and willingness to trust the right people with responsibility are essential to every rebuilding project. Great works are accomplished not just by builders but by the people who equip them.
strengths: Generosity with resources, time, influence, and opportunity
Ability to recognize trustworthy people and empower them with authority
Willingness to change course when presented with compelling reasons
Positional influence that can open doors no one else can open
watchFor: Using your power to control rather than empower
Failing to follow up on the projects and people you have resourced
Making decisions based on whoever speaks to you last rather than on principle
Assuming that providing resources is a substitute for personal involvement in God's work

scripture.text: In the Lord's hand the king's heart is a stream of water that he channels toward all who please him.

results.title: The Spiritual Foundation Builder
results.description: You are an Ezra — someone who knows that lasting change must be rooted in the Word of God. While others focus on the visible structures, you focus on the invisible foundations. You understand that rebuilt walls without rebuilt hearts will not endure, and your gift is bringing people back to Scripture, helping them understand it, and leading them into the kind of spiritual renewal that sustains every other form of rebuilding. You teach, mentor, and model a life shaped by God's truth.
strengths: Deep knowledge of Scripture and ability to apply it to real-life situations
Gift for teaching and making complex truths accessible to others
Commitment to personal integrity — practicing what you teach
Ability to shepherd people through conviction to joy without leaving them in guilt
watchFor: Becoming so focused on study that you neglect practical action
Using knowledge as a source of pride rather than a tool for service
Expecting others to have the same depth of devotion before they have had time to grow
Retreating into the safety of scholarship when the situation requires bold, public action

scripture.text: For Ezra had devoted himself to the study and observance of the Law of the Lord, and to teaching its decrees and laws in Israel.
